title: Deep dives, bottlenecks and trade-offs

kcs.statement: A bottleneck is the component that saturates first as load grows; you find it by comparing peak qps, storage and bandwidth estimates against what one instance of each component can handle.
In the deep dive, pick the one or two components with the hardest requirement (highest load or strictest consistency) and detail them instead of spreading time evenly.
Every design choice is stated as a trade-off naming what is gained and what is given up (e.g. lower latency for staler data).

problem_ideas: A single database handles 5,000 QPS but peak reads are 40,000: name the bottleneck and the next question to ask
Choose the deep-dive component for a URL shortener vs for a chat app and justify
Rewrite 'use NoSQL because it scales' as an explicit trade-off
Rank three components in a feed design by which saturates first
Interviewer asks 'what breaks at 10× traffic?': produce a structured answer
Spot the design whose bottleneck is bandwidth rather than QPS
